method: E12b recipe + pseudo-labelling (semi-supervised): test images predicted with >=0.99 confidence by the E13v ensemble (trained on the 80% split only) are added to training with their predicted class
explanation: Val accuracy 0.977 vs 0.972 for E12b (55 -> 45 errors), single change = 9046 pseudo-labelled test images. Gain is uniform across 72 px and large files. BUT inside the 3-model ensemble it brings nothing (E8+E16+E13 = E8+E12b+E13 = 0.981): the pseudo-labels come from that same ensemble, so E16 mostly learns to imitate it (self-distillation) - the single model catches up with the ensemble rather than surpassing it, and members become more correlated.
preprocessing: Alpha-composite on white background, then resize to 144x144 with NEAREST neighbour, ImageNet normalisation
preprocessing_why: Single change vs E12b: ~9000 extra (unlabelled) test images. On validation, predictions with >=0.99 confidence cover 91.5% of images and are 99.7% correct, so the added labels are almost noise-free. Pseudo-labels come from models that never saw the validation split -> validation score stays unbiased.
